- Overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate prices during sharp downward trends; adjust upward to reflect stronger-than-expected demand or policy effects.
- Overshoot after high historical peaks; cap forecasts at 10–15% below the peak to avoid overreaction.
- Mean-revert toward historical 30-day average if forecast deviates >15% from recent trend; use rolling average as anchor.
- Lag in response to true price drops; delay forecast correction by 1–2 days to match actual market reaction.
- Avoid overfitting to recent volatility; smooth out erratic short-term swings with exponential decay filter (e.g., 0.8 decay factor).
